newsitem.title: UK: IPE implements first gas oil delivery changes. [CORRECTED 17:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: IPE implements first gas oil delivery changes. [CORRECTED 17:00 GMT]

text.p: The International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) implemented the first of several planned reforms of gas oil trade on Thursday, tightening delivery procedures in line with an independent review of the contract earlier this year.

The IPE said in a letter to members three amendments to gas oil delivery regulations took effect immediately because what it called insufficient objections had been received from members during a consultation period.

The letter, faxed later to media organisations, said seven amendments had been approved including a much-discussed change to rule J11 which in effect stipulates that shorts (corrects from longs) must have proof of oil in tank when making delivery after each month's contract expiry.
The letter added that some concern had been registered by members about the change to rule J11, as well as about amendments to rules K5 and K6.
The seven approved changes are part of reforms agreed in principle in May by the IPE board of directors and due to take effect in stages during the rest of this year.

Market observers have said the proposed new IPE rules reflect an attempt to strike a balance between keeping traded volumes at a healthy level while guarding against potentially damaging speculative squeezes which can disrupt physical trade.
The most controversial changes involve limits on traders holding large positions ahead of each month's gas oil contract expiry. these are likely to be reviewed, officials say.
